title: [VSC-23] VS Code task detail: refresh the Delivery section and Release Agent button live, and pin blocker labels to MoeBundle
description:
Filed by VSC-18 (task-43363b5d) from its adversarial pass over the epic diff.
1. The Delivery section (VSC-8) and the Release Agent button (VSC-11) are rendered only in the initial HTML (TaskDetailPanel.getWebviewContent). The live path, debouncedUpdate posting 'updateTask' to media/taskDetail.js (around line 336), rebuilds only the status badge, #blockerSection, the plan and the comments. So a candidate, check run or receipt recorded while the panel is open stays stale until it is reopened. A task assigned after the panel opened gets no Release Agent button, and a released one keeps a stale button (that click answers with the info message). JetBrains refreshes its delivery section on every state update (TaskDetailDialog.refreshDeliverySection). Fix idea from architect comment-97b50ba7 on VSC-18: the panel posts the precomputed deliveryRows and labels with 'updateTask', and taskDetail.js rebuilds an always-present #deliverySection from DOM text nodes, as renderBlocker does. Do the same for the button's visibility.
2. BLOCK_CAUSE_LABEL and BLOCK_CAUSE_CLEARS exist in 3 VS Code copies: TaskDetailPanel.ts, media/board.js and media/taskDetail.js. They equal moe.blocker.* in MoeBundle.properties today, but no test pins that: tests/blocker-corpus.test.cjs compares the chip with the panel's own constant. Add a bundle-equality assertion, as delivery-corpus does for moe.delivery.*.
definitionOfDone: With the panel open, an 'updateTask' carrying new delivery evidence re-renders #deliverySection, and one without delivery removes it. A node:test drives the real panel and the raw media/taskDetail.js in vm, every daemon string goes through text nodes or escapeHtml, and the test proves it.
The Release Agent button appears or disappears on a live 'updateTask' when assignedWorkerId changes, with a test.
A test asserts that the blocker cause and clearance labels in all 3 VS Code copies equal moe.blocker.* in MoeBundle.properties.
In a git-archive snapshot, moe-vscode `npm ci && npm run lint && npm run compile && npm test` exits 0 and no existing test is weakened.

implementationPlan.description: 1. Tests first (RED). Write tool only; never cp into the checkout. Create moe-vscode/tests/task-detail-live.test.cjs (node:test, no new dependency: npm test's tests/*.test.cjs glob picks it up). A reference implementation of this exact design passed the full snapshot gate and all three checkRefs at ed60ab31: /mnt/d/moe-scratch/vsc23-prototype/moe-vscode/tests/task-detail-live.test.cjs (read it, then write the tracked file with the Write tool). Harness: production source only, nothing re-implemented. - Extension side: transpile src/panels/TaskDetailPanel.ts and src/panels/PlanReviewPanel.ts with ts.transpileModule (CommonJS, ES2020, esModuleInterop). Run them under node:vm with a strict require map: vscode and './PlanReviewPanel' only, anything else throws (mem:gotcha-vscode-panel-strict-require-map). - The panel's vm context also needs a recording setTimeout and a no-op clearTimeout. debouncedUpdate arms a 200 ms timer, and a vm context has no timers of its own. - openPanel(task) loads a fresh module each time, because the panel keeps a static map. It opens the panel with TaskDetailPanel.createOrShow and keeps the onStateChanged listener and every webview.postMessage call. - update(next) replaces the task in the client state, fires the listener and runs the recorded timer. It asserts exactly one posted message of type 'updateTask' and returns it JSON-round-tripped. That is what a webview receives, and it carries no vm-realm prototypes. - Page side: run the raw media/taskDetail.js in a fresh vm context per page. Supply acquireVsCodeApi with a recording postMessage, document { getElementById, createElement, createTextNode }, and window.addEventListener capturing the 'message' handler (throw if none was registered). - The page is built from the panel's real initial HTML. Every id="..." becomes an element, in document order: children of a main-content element until #actionsBar, children of #actionsBar after it. #initial-data gets the tag's data-* attributes as its dataset, following tests/task-release.test.cjs initialDataset. - The DOM fake is strict in both directions, and that is how this file proves every daemon string reaches the page as text. Each node is a Proxy: get throws on a member the node lacks, and set throws on any property outside the allowlist className, id, title, textContent, value, scrollTop. - So the markup-injection DOM property the forbidden-pattern rail greps for, and outerHTML, throw without this file ever naming them. Never spell any globalRails.forbiddenPatterns token in the test. - getElementById walks the tree from the body and answers null for an id that is not attached, as a real DOM does. - Nodes keep parentNode, children, nextSibling, appendChild, insertBefore (a reference that is not a child throws), removeChild (a non-child throws), addEventListener and click(). Tests: keep these exact name prefixes, because checkref 2 greps 'not ok N - L1:' and 'not ok N - L4:'. - L0: harness self-check. Writing outerHTML on #blockerSection throws (refused write). Reading an unknown member throws. getElementById answers null for #deliverySection and #releaseAgentBtn on an unassigned task with no delivery. - L1: replay every row of moe-jetbrains/src/test/resources/client-delivery.json. That corpus is read-only: never edit it. - For each row, open the panel on a task with no delivery and deliver update(task with row.delivery) to the page. - Read the live #deliverySection as { title, rows: [className, label text, value title, value text] }. - It must equal the same read of the initial markup of a panel opened directly on that delivery. Both are null when there are no rows. - Collect failures as ': expected ..., got ...' and assert the list empty. - L2: run it for a page that starts without a delivery and for one that starts with one. - After each of two successive deliveries there is exactly one #deliverySection, immediately after #blockerSection in its parent, matching the initial markup. - Then a task with delivery:null removes it (getElementById answers null), and so does a task without the member. - Values typed into titleInput, descriptionInput and dodInput before the updates are unchanged after them. - L3: use a hostile runner string such as ' & \'quoted\'' as the check command and as the receipt target. - The posted message carries it unescaped in value and fullValue. The page writes text, so escaping in the message would double-escape. - Each live value node has textContent and title equal to the raw string, and no child nodes. - L4: run it for a page that starts unassigned and one that starts assigned, over a sequence of assignedWorkerId values: non-blank ids, null, '', whitespace and absent. - The posted releaseAgentLabel is the bundle's moe.button.releaseAgent text exactly when the id is non-blank, else null. Read that text from MoeBundle.properties; never copy it. - After each delivery, #releaseAgentBtn is absent for a blank id. Otherwise there is exactly one, immediately before #prevBtn. - A button that was already shown is the same node afterwards, never rebuilt. - A button built live reproduces the initial render's element. Compare its tagName, className and text with a panel opened on that assignment. - Finally, one click posts exactly [{type:'releaseAgent'}]. RED: run the new file against HEAD's sources in a scratch copy outside the checkout (git show HEAD: into a mktemp dir with the same layout, then NODE_PATH=/moe-vscode/node_modules node --test ; mem:convention-vscode-renderer-tests). L1 to L4 fail and L0 passes. Size: target at most 265 lines for this file. The prototype is 256.

implementationPlan.description:
2. Panel, Edit tool only: moe-vscode/src/panels/TaskDetailPanel.ts. Add no new import: several test files load this panel through closed require maps (mem:gotcha-vscode-panel-strict-require-map). Prototype: /mnt/d/moe-scratch/vsc23-prototype/moe-vscode/src/panels/TaskDetailPanel.ts.

- Directly after deliveryRows, add `export function deliveryDisplay(delivery: unknown)` returning { title: DELIVERY_LABELS[DELIVERY_TITLE_KEY], rows: deliveryRows(delivery).map(row => ({ ...row, label: DELIVERY_LABELS[row.labelKey] ?? row.labelKey })) }.
  - This is the one label lookup behind both renderers.
  - The text stays raw: the initial markup escapes it, and the page writes it as DOM text.
- renderDelivery(task) builds from deliveryDisplay(task.delivery) and emits byte-identical markup. escapeHtml stays on title, label, fullValue and value. tests/delivery-corpus.test.cjs pins this markup and must stay unchanged.
- Beside the other Release Agent constants, add the module-level `function releaseAgentLabel(task: Task): string | null`. It returns nonBlankString(task.assignedWorkerId) !== null ? RELEASE_AGENT_LABEL : null.
  - The actions-bar button condition in getWebviewContent uses it. The button markup is unchanged.
- debouncedUpdate posts { type: 'updateTask', task, delivery: deliveryDisplay(task.delivery), releaseAgentLabel: releaseAgentLabel(task) }.
- Keep the 'releaseAgent' message handler's fresh-state check and its 'No agent is assigned to this task.' info message, because a click can still race a live update. Reword three comments:
  - the handler's comment, because 'the actions bar is static' is no longer true;
  - the HTML comment above ${this.renderDelivery(task)}: 'rendered once ... no live refresh yet' becomes live-refreshed by media/taskDetail.js;
  - renderDelivery's doc comment.

Error handling: deliveryRows is already total (a malformed delivery yields no rows), so deliveryDisplay cannot throw, and this step adds no new failure path.

Size: net at most +20 lines. The prototype is +28/-10.

implementationPlan.description:
3. Page, Edit tool only: moe-vscode/media/taskDetail.js. Prototype: /mnt/d/moe-scratch/vsc23-prototype/moe-vscode/media/taskDetail.js. Keep renderDelivery and renderReleaseAgent as top-level function declarations with exactly these names, never `var x = function`, because checkref 2 overrides each one by appending a same-named declaration.

- Extract `function postReleaseAgent() { vscodeApi.postMessage({ type: 'releaseAgent' }); }` and attach it at load to an existing #releaseAgentBtn, as today.
- `function removeNode(node)` detaches a node only when node && node.parentNode. The guard is load-bearing.
  - tests/task-blocker-visibility.test.cjs and tests/approval-paths.test.cjs deliver old-shape updateTask messages, which carry no delivery and no releaseAgentLabel. Their fakes return a parentless node for every id.
  - Both files must pass unchanged, including task-blocker-visibility's touched-set assertion: exactly blockerSection, commentsList, planContent and statusBadge.
  - So a message with no delivery rows and no label may only remove attached nodes. It must never write to an existing element.
- `function renderDelivery(delivery)`:
  - rows = delivery && Array.isArray(delivery.rows) ? the rows that are non-null objects : [].
  - No rows: removeNode(#deliverySection).
  - Otherwise reuse #deliverySection, or create div.delivery-section#deliverySection and insert it right after #blockerSection with blocker.parentNode.insertBefore(section, blocker.nextSibling). Do nothing if #blockerSection is missing or detached.
  - Clear the section with textContent = '', then append the title line, blockerLine('section-title', title).
  - For each row, append a div whose className is 'delivery-row', plus ' delivery-pass' for outcome 'PASS' or ' delivery-fail' for 'FAIL' (nothing for any other value). It holds blockerLine('field-label', label) and blockerLine('delivery-value', value), and the value node's title property is set to fullValue.
  - Node order and classes match TaskDetailPanel.renderDelivery.
- `function renderReleaseAgent(label)`:
  - A non-string or empty label: removeNode(#releaseAgentBtn).
  - A button that is already shown stays as it is, with no second listener.
  - Otherwise create a button with className 'btn btn-secondary', id 'releaseAgentBtn' and textContent = label. Its click calls postReleaseAgent. Insert it before #prevBtn in its parent; do nothing if #prevBtn is missing or detached.
- In the 'updateTask' branch, call renderDelivery(msg.delivery) and then renderReleaseAgent(msg.releaseAgentLabel) LAST, after renderComments, so nothing new can hold up the renderedPlanRevision assignment. Update the handler's header comment ('only update plan + comments').

Error handling: a missing, null or malformed delivery, rows list, row or label never throws. It renders no section and no button. Text only ever goes in through textContent or the title property, never through markup.

Size: net at most +62 lines. The prototype is +65/-7. L0 to L4 now pass.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
1. An always-present #deliverySection wrapper (the idea in comment-97b50ba7). Rejected because tests/delivery-corpus.test.cjs asserts that a task without delivery renders no 'deliverySection' at all, and DoD 1 says an update without delivery removes the section. Instead, live mirrors the initial render: the section is created after #blockerSection when there are rows and removed when there are none.
2. Always rendering the Release Agent button and hiding it. Rejected because task-release.test.cjs asserts that an unassigned page has no releaseAgentBtn. The button is created and removed instead.
3. A fourth copy of deliveryRows in the page script. Rejected: the panel resolves the rows and labels once, in the new deliveryDisplay, and posts them.
4. Having the page derive button visibility from task.assignedWorkerId. Rejected: the panel posts releaseAgentLabel, so there is one rule (releaseAgentLabel(task), also used by the initial HTML) and no copy of the label in the page.
5. Fixing the docs here. Deferred: moe-vscode/README.md Known issues line 71 and MANUAL_TESTS.md step 6 describe this limit, but they are VSC-18's open paths (REVIEW). A docs follow-up drops them, which keeps this row at 4 files.
JetBrains parity: TaskDetailDialog.refreshDeliverySection rebuilds delivery on every state update, which this row matches. JetBrains builds its modal's Release Agent action once, so a live button is VS Code-only and needs no corpus row; both clients use the same visibility rule, a non-blank assignedWorkerId.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- A node:vm context has no setTimeout. The panel's debouncedUpdate needs one injected into its context.
- media/board.js declares its blocker constants with top-level const (lines 26-37). Those are readable through vm.runInContext(name, ctx), never as context properties. taskDetail.js uses var (lines 47-65).
- Node 24's node --test uses the spec reporter even when piped. The mutant checkRefs force --test-reporter=tap so they can grep 'not ok N - L1:'.
- Two existing files send old-shape updateTask messages: task-blocker-visibility.test.cjs (lazily created parentless nodes, plus a touched-set assertion at line 547) and approval-paths.test.cjs (plain nodes). That is why removal is guarded by parentNode and why an empty update never writes to an existing element.
- Several test files load TaskDetailPanel with closed require maps, so the panel gets no new import.
- I built a full prototype at /mnt/d/moe-scratch/vsc23-prototype (base ed60ab31; none of the involved paths changed since c02dc7cb). It passed lint, compile and npm test at 562/558/4 skip/0 fail, and all three checkRefs. Negative controls fail each checkRef: removing C3, skipping board.js in C3, and a vacuous L1 or L4. Treat it as a reference only: write the tracked files with the Edit/Write tools.

- Spelling the markup-injection property in the test trips the forbidden-pattern rail. The allowlisting set trap covers it without naming it.
- A second click listener on a kept button, or a section appended at the end of the page instead of after #blockerSection.
